<reason>B narrowly wins on the motion’s permissive decision rule. A convincingly defended fixed rewards with affordable supply and exposed B’s unsupported claim that these require upfront payment for possible failure. But demonstrating a preferable contract did not establish why countries should reject a high-price commitment when alternative terms cannot be secured. B combined A’s explicit willingness to walk away with central reimbursement and the clinical value of reserve availability. A’s budget and sales-incentive objections remained substantial, but distinguishing emergency purchasing from advance guarantees did not fully answer the risk of losing development or continued supply.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest move was using A’s walk-away answer to distinguish permitting a fallback from preferring its pricing structure. That preserved B’s route despite A’s effective rebuttal that equal expected compensation need not require high marginal charges.</best_rebuttal>
